data.narrative:
K2 Space, a Series D-stage space and aerospace company that has raised $500M to date, is valued here using a triangulated framework anchored to two applicable methods. The peer set consists of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies—Sierra Space ($8.0B Series C), Apex Space ($2.3B Series D), Varda Space Industries ($1.6B Series D), and Skyryse ($1.1B Series C)—alongside five public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) that trade at a median 27.4x price-to-sales.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier to the $500M raised proxy, implying a $750M valuation. Peer-median anchoring across the four private comps yields a $1.9B implied value, with a range spanning $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp P/S anchoring cannot be applied due to the absence of target revenue disclosure, a common constraint for private companies. These two methods triangulate to a low of $638M, median of $1.3B, and high of $2.2B.

Key uncertainties include material dispersion in the peer set—particularly Sierra Space's $8.0B valuation at the Series C stage—and the absence of revenue or unit-economics data to calibrate public-multiple approaches. The $1.3B median reflects current-stage pricing; K2's actual valuation will depend on revenue growth trajectory and capital efficiency relative to demonstrated peers.
